title: The opposite of a triangulated category is triangulated
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Equip $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$ with the shift $(\operatorname{op}X)[n]=\operatorname{op}(X[-n])$ for every $n\in\mathbf Z$. Declare its distinguished triangles to be the triangles isomorphic to $\operatorname{op}Z\to\operatorname{op}Y\to\operatorname{op}X\to(\operatorname{op}Z)[1]$ obtained by reversing distinguished triangles $X\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}Z\xrightarrow{w}X[1]$ of $\mathcal C$: the first two maps are $v^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $u^{\mathrm{op}}$, and the last is the opposite of $w[-1]:Z[-1]\to X$, using the shift-identification $X[1][-1]\cong X$, with no additional minus sign. With these structures $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a triangulated category. No smallness, boundedness or idempotent-completeness hypothesis is required.
